elements.content: Grammar focus: B2 Master Review.

In an exam, read the instruction before the sentence: transformation tasks name the structure (begin with Not only, rewrite using a noun phrase), while reformulation tasks only fix the meaning. Then check three things in order - verb form, information order, stance - because that is the order markers are lost.

verb forms — subjunctive, conditionals, passives: It is essential that he be informed
information order — fronting, inversion, clefts: Rarely has the board seen such a split
compression — nominalisation, ellipsis, substitution: The implementation of the policy took two years
stance — hedging, concession, rhetoric: The proposal is arguably the safest
reformulation — clause to noun phrase: When we automate → the automation of
transformation — same meaning, required structure: Not only did costs rise...
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which task type fixes only the meaning?
2. Complete: 'Under no circumstances ___ the data be shared.'
3. What do you check first in a transformation answer?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

Mandative subjunctive — It is essential that he be informed. (Base verb after demand verbs.)
Distancing passive — The report is said to reflect a trend. (Agent removed, claim reported.)
Inversion — Rarely has the board seen such a split. (Negative fronting inverts.)
Hedging — The proposal is arguably the safest. (Claim marked as debatable.)
What do you observe?

The B2 system has four families. Verb forms: mandative subjunctive, mixed conditionals, distancing passives, reporting patterns. Information order: fronting, inversion, cleft sentences. Compression and register: nominalisation, ellipsis, substitution. Stance: hedging, concession, rhetorical structure. An exam task rarely tests one family alone: a reformulation task asks you to move a clause into a noun phrase, and a transformation task asks you to invert after a negative adverb.
1. Which family does 'Rarely has the board seen' belong to?
2. What does a distancing passive do?
options: Reports a claim without naming the source.

Freer production: Can demonstrate full B2 upper-intermediate/vantage level mastery across executive, academic, geopolitical, and socio-cultural scenarios

Success criteria:
- I can name the four families of B2 structure.
- I can transform a sentence to a required structure and keep the meaning.
- I can check verb form, order and stance before I submit.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ Not only the costs rose but quality fell (inversion missing) → ✅ Not only did the costs rise, but quality fell
❌ It is essential that he is informed (indicative after a mandative verb) → ✅ It is essential that he be informed
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The committee demanded that the figures be released.
Under no circumstances should the data be shared.
The refusal to publish delayed the audit.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where confusing grammar: pairs that look alike carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Confusing Grammar: Pairs that Look Alike. For each pair, learn the single point that separates them, then test the sentence against that point: is the meaning past or present, duty or memory, preference or warning? The for
